purpose: A bounded, verifiable method for autonomously assembling a near-complete census of independent (non-chain) businesses in Turlock, CA by ingesting and reliability-ranking multiple public sources, resolving and deduplicating entities across them, classifying each by independence and premise type, verifying that each is currently active and inside the geographic boundary, attaching per-record provenance and source-agreement confidence, estimating remaining coverage via capture-recapture, modeling revenue only as a labeled benchmark estimate (never as fact), and gating each finished record into categorization with a definition-of-done.
assumptions: only public business data and public records (e.g. county FBN filings, city business-tax certificates) are used; no private or personal owner data beyond what those public records expose
the target geography is the City of Turlock, Stanislaus County, California, ZIP 95380 and 95382, plus a labeled greater-Turlock fringe of unincorporated edges
per-business revenue for a private shop is not public; revenue is modeled only as an explicitly labeled industry-benchmark estimate, never stated as an actual dollar figure for a named business
sources are accessed in accordance with their terms of service; bot-blocked or JS-rendered pages are handled by lawful triangulation rather than circumvention
the census is a point-in-time artifact that goes stale and must be re-verified on a cadence; completeness is estimated, not assumed
exclusions: categorizing or tagging businesses by line of trade — that is the downstream categorization KB this one hands off to
scoring, ranking, or recommending businesses for any commercial purpose
collecting private personal data about owners (home address, finances, family) beyond what a public FBN or tax-certificate filing already discloses
national chains, franchises, and corporate-owned outlets except as the explicit out-of-scope class the independence filter removes
businesses wholly outside the defined Turlock geographic boundary

competency_questions.question: What exactly is the census trying to capture, and how do we know when it is complete enough to stop?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CENSUS_GOAL defines the in-scope universe and a bounded stop condition; COVERAGE_ESTIMATION supplies the completeness estimate that decides when to stop

competency_questions.question: Which public sources exist, and how trustworthy is each for discovering independent Turlock businesses?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SOURCE_INVENTORY enumerates the sources and assigns each a reliability rank with the bias it carries

competency_questions.question: How are the authoritative curated seeds (Chamber directory, Downtown association list) ingested, and why is neither sufficient alone?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CHAMBER_SEED and DOWNTOWN_LIST describe ingestion and the membership/footprint coverage gap each leaves

competency_questions.question: How do county FBN filings and city business-tax certificates serve as ownership and licensing ground-truth?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FBN_OWNERSHIP links DBA to owner from filings and TAX_CERT_LAYER describes the licensing census and how to request it

competency_questions.question: How are crowd directories and social platforms harvested without importing chain and stale-listing bias, and what is done when a source is bot-blocked, returns HTTP 403, or renders only via JavaScript?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CROWD_DIRECTORIES and SOCIAL_SIGNALS explain harvesting with bias correction and existence/freshness signals, and BLOCKED_SOURCE_TACTICS lists the lawful fallbacks (snippet triangulation, cached views, mirrors, manual capture)

competency_questions.question: How are the same business's records from different sources merged into one without false merges or splits?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ENTITY_RESOLUTION specifies name/address/phone normalization and the fuzzy-match plus blocking rule

competency_questions.question: How is an independent business distinguished from a chain or franchise so only in-scope entities are kept?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INDIE_VS_CHAIN gives the operational signals and the keep/drop rule for the independence filter

competency_questions.question: How is a record classified as storefront, home-based, or mobile/service-area, and how are sibling locations under one owner consolidated?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PREMISE_TYPE_CLASS defines the three premise types and their verification paths and MULTILOC_CONSOLIDATION links sibling locations to one owner while keeping each premise distinct

competency_questions.question: How is a business verified as currently active versus closed or defunct?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ACTIVE_VS_CLOSED lists the freshness signals and the rule that marks a record active, dormant, or closed

competency_questions.question: What geographic boundary counts as Turlock, and how are unincorporated and ZIP-edge cases decided?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GEO_BOUNDARY defines city limits, the 95380/95382 ZIPs, and the labeled greater-Turlock fringe rule

competency_questions.question: What must each record contain before it is allowed forward, how is its provenance and source-agreement confidence recorded, and how is revenue represented honestly?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROVENANCE_CONFIDENCE attaches per-field sources and a confidence label, RECORD_SCHEMA defines the canonical required fields, and REVENUE_ESTIMATION represents revenue only as a labeled benchmark estimate with confidence and a confirmation path

competency_questions.question: What are the legal and ethical limits on which data may be collected and from where?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SOURCING_ETHICS states the public-data-only rule, ToS respect, and the prohibition on private owner data

competency_questions.question: How does the catalog stay current as businesses open, move, and close, and what definition-of-done lets a verified record pass to categorization?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FRESHNESS_CADENCE sets the re-verification cadence and staleness triggers and HANDOFF_GATE states the pass conditions a record must meet before it leaves discovery

glossary.definition: A statement filed with the Stanislaus County Clerk-Recorder when a business operates under a name other than the owner's legal name; the public filing links a DBA to its registrant(s) and a filing date, serving as ownership ground-truth.

The City of Turlock's business license/tax registration that nearly every business operating in city limits must hold; the roster (obtainable by public-records request) is the closest thing to a licensing census of in-city businesses.

An estimation technique borrowed from ecology: counting how many businesses appear in two independent source lists and how many overlap lets you estimate the total population, including the unseen tail neither list captured.

The process of deciding that two records from different sources refer to the same real-world business (or that they do not), using normalized name, address, and phone plus fuzzy matching within blocking keys.
A coarse grouping (e.g. normalized street number plus ZIP, or phone area+prefix) used to limit fuzzy comparison to plausible candidate pairs instead of comparing every record against every other.

Whether a business operates from a public-facing storefront, from a residence (home-based), or as a mobile/service-area operator with no fixed customer-facing address; it changes how the business is found and verified.

Reconstructing a fact from a blocked or JS-only page using the search-engine result snippet, the page title, and corroborating mentions on other reachable pages, instead of loading the blocked page itself.
A per-record confidence label derived from how many independent sources corroborate the same name, address, and status, and from the reliability rank of those sources.

An industry-average ratio of annual revenue to headcount (or to square footage) published for a sector; multiplied by an observable size signal it yields a labeled revenue estimate band, never an actual figure for a named shop.

A discovery target that aims to enumerate essentially all in-scope independent businesses, accepting a small estimated unseen tail, with the completeness percentage itself reported as a measured quantity.

nodes.definition: Fix the discovery target as a near-complete census of every independent, currently-operating business physically located in Turlock, with an explicit stop condition rather than an open-ended crawl. The in-scope universe is defined positively (independent, active, inside the boundary) and the run ends when capture-recapture estimates remaining unseen businesses below a stated threshold and the curated and licensing layers are both exhausted.

pros.claim: A stated stop condition prevents an unbounded crawl that never declares completeness
pros.example: stopping when capture-recapture estimates fewer than ~5% of independents unseen and the city certificate roster is fully reconciled

cons.claim: A fixed completeness threshold can declare done while a whole hard-to-find class (home-based) stays underrepresented
cons.example: hitting 95% on storefronts while mobile detailers remain mostly invisible

failure_modes: treating discovery as endless so it never hands off
defining scope so loosely that chains and out-of-town entities leak in
acceptance_tests: the goal states the positive in-scope test, the geographic and independence filters by reference, and a numeric completeness stop condition
revisit_triggers: the sponsor changes the in-scope definition
the completeness threshold proves unreachable for a business class

base.update_signal: the in-scope definition or completeness threshold is restated

nodes.definition: Enumerate and reliability-rank every public source feeding the census: City of Turlock business-tax certificates and county FBN filings as authoritative ground-truth; the Chamber member directory and Downtown association list as curated but partial seeds; Google Maps/Places, Yelp, and YellowPages as broad but chain-polluted and stale-prone crowd directories; OpenStreetMap as a sparse but clean geo layer; and Instagram, Facebook, and NextDoor as freshness and existence signals only. Each source gets a rank, its known bias, and the role it is trusted for.

included: the role each source is trusted for
excluded: the ingestion mechanics of any one source

pros.claim: Ranking sources by reliability stops a single noisy directory from outvoting authoritative records
pros.example: a city tax-certificate entry overriding a stale Yelp 'permanently closed' flag

cons.claim: A fixed ranking can be wrong for a specific field where a low-ranked source is actually best
cons.example: Instagram being the freshest signal that a downtown cafe is still open this week

failure_modes: treating every source as equally trustworthy and merging garbage
omitting the licensing layer and missing businesses no directory lists
acceptance_tests: each named source has a reliability rank, its dominant bias, and the specific role (ground-truth, seed, breadth, or freshness signal) it is assigned
revisit_triggers: a source goes offline, changes access policy, or proves systematically wrong
a new public source becomes available

base.update_signal: a source's availability, access policy, or trustworthiness changes

nodes.definition: Bind the whole pipeline to public business data only, accessed within each source's terms of service. The rule set: ingest only information a business or a public agency has published; respect robots and rate limits rather than circumventing anti-bot controls; never collect private personal data about owners beyond what a public FBN or tax-certificate filing already exposes; and treat any private/personal detail (home address used only as a residence, family, finances) as out of scope even when technically reachable.

included: owner privacy boundary beyond public records

pros.claim: A bright-line public-only rule keeps the census defensible and avoids privacy and ToS liability
pros.example: publishing an FBN registrant name but never the owner's unrelated home phone scraped elsewhere

cons.claim: The strict boundary leaves some genuinely useful owner-linkage signals on the table
cons.example: declining to cross-reference a personal social profile that would confirm ownership

failure_modes: scraping a source in violation of its ToS to fill a gap
recording private owner details a public record never disclosed
acceptance_tests: every collected field traces to a public source, no source was accessed against its ToS, and no private owner datum beyond public records is stored
revisit_triggers: a source's ToS changes
a new privacy regulation alters what public data may be retained

base.update_signal: a source ToS or privacy rule that governs collection changes

nodes.definition: Define what counts as Turlock so a record's location decides inclusion deterministically. The core is the incorporated City of Turlock limits; the practical net is ZIP 95380 and 95382; and a labeled greater-Turlock fringe covers unincorporated Stanislaus pockets that share the Turlock identity and mailing city. Each record carries a boundary tag (in-city, in-ZIP, or fringe) so downstream consumers can include or exclude the fringe explicitly.

pros.claim: A boundary tag per record lets the fringe be included or dropped without re-running discovery
pros.example: excluding an unincorporated almond-huller that mails as Turlock when only in-city retail is wanted

cons.claim: ZIP boundaries and city limits disagree, so any single rule mis-tags edge addresses
cons.example: a 95380 address that sits in unincorporated county, not the city

failure_modes: using ZIP as a proxy for city limits and over-including fringe businesses silently
dropping a legitimately in-city business whose listing shows a neighboring town
acceptance_tests: each record carries an explicit boundary tag (in-city / in-ZIP / fringe) and the tag rule is documented against city limits and the 95380/95382 ZIPs
revisit_triggers: an annexation changes city limits
a ZIP boundary is redrawn

base.update_signal: city limits or ZIP boundaries change

nodes.definition: Ingest the Turlock Chamber of Commerce member directory as the first authoritative, human-curated seed: it is categorized, address- and phone-bearing, and almost entirely real local businesses. Its hard limit is that membership is voluntary and paid, so it captures perhaps a minority of all businesses and skews toward established, civic-minded firms; it is a high-precision, low-recall seed that must be supplemented, never treated as the universe.

pros.claim: The Chamber directory yields clean, real, pre-categorized seeds that anchor entity resolution
pros.example: a member entry with verified name, suite, and phone becomes a high-confidence anchor record

cons.claim: Membership bias means whole swaths of newer or smaller independents are simply absent
cons.example: a one-year-old home-based bakery that never joined the Chamber

failure_modes: mistaking the member list for the full population and under-searching
carrying a lapsed member as active without re-verification
acceptance_tests: member records are ingested with name, address, phone, and source tag, and the run records that this layer is high-precision but partial
revisit_triggers: the Chamber publishes an updated directory
membership terms or directory format change

base.update_signal: the Chamber member directory is republished or restructured

nodes.definition: Ingest the Downtown Turlock Property Owners Association / shopdowntownturlock business listing as a dense, high-precision seed for the independent retail, dining, and service core where chains are sparse and independents cluster. It covers a small geographic footprint exhaustively, complementing the Chamber's breadth; its limit is exactly that footprint — it says nothing about businesses outside the downtown district.

included: dense independent coverage of a small footprint

pros.claim: The downtown list near-exhaustively captures the densest cluster of independents in one pass
pros.example: an entire block of Main Street independents enumerated where Yelp shows gaps

cons.claim: Its tight footprint gives a false sense of completeness if mistaken for citywide coverage
cons.example: treating full downtown coverage as 90% of all Turlock independents

failure_modes: promotional listings that include a temporary pop-up as a permanent business
assuming downtown completeness generalizes citywide
acceptance_tests: downtown-district businesses are ingested with name, address, and source tag, and the record set is marked footprint-bounded to the downtown district
revisit_triggers: the association republishes its directory
the downtown district boundary is redrawn

base.update_signal: the downtown association listing is republished

nodes.definition: Add the City of Turlock business-tax certificate roster as the licensing census — the single source closest to enumerating every business operating in city limits, because nearly all must register. Obtain it via a public-records request to the city (the roster is public though some fields may be withheld), then reconcile it against the directory seeds: certificate-only entries are businesses no directory listed, and directory-only entries flag possible unlicensed, closed, or fringe cases.

pros.claim: The certificate roster surfaces the long tail of businesses that no public directory ever lists
pros.example: a home-based bookkeeper holding a city certificate but absent from Yelp, Google, and the Chamber

cons.claim: The roster lags real status and may withhold fields, so it needs cross-verification
cons.example: a certificate still on file months after the shop quietly closed

failure_modes: treating a stale certificate as proof a business is still active
failing to request the roster and missing the licensing layer entirely
acceptance_tests: the city certificate roster is obtained via documented public-records request and reconciled against the seeds, producing certificate-only and directory-only difference lists
revisit_triggers: the city publishes an updated roster
the public-records request process or released fields change

base.update_signal: the city certificate roster is reissued or its released fields change

nodes.definition: Use Stanislaus County FBN (fictitious business name) filings as ownership ground-truth: each public statement links a DBA to its registrant name(s), business address, and filing/expiration date. This resolves who actually owns a trade name, distinguishes independents from corporate DBAs, and powers single-owner multi-location consolidation. Only the public filing fields are used; no private owner data beyond the registrant information the filing itself discloses.

included: filing date and expiry as activity signal
excluded: private owner data beyond the filing

pros.claim: FBN filings authoritatively tie a trade name to an owner, enabling correct multi-location grouping
pros.example: two differently-named storefronts shown to share one registrant on file

cons.claim: FBN data is lumpy: not every business files, filings expire, and registrants can be holding entities
cons.example: an active independent that never filed an FBN because it trades under the owner's legal name

failure_modes: assuming every business has an FBN and dropping those that lawfully do not
treating an expired FBN as proof of closure
acceptance_tests: matched records carry the FBN registrant linkage and filing date, and absence of an FBN is recorded as unknown rather than disqualifying
revisit_triggers: a new FBN filing or renewal posts for a tracked name
the county changes how filings are published

base.update_signal: a tracked business's FBN filing posts, renews, or lapses

nodes.definition: Harvest the broad crowd directories — Google Maps/Places, Yelp, YellowPages, and OpenStreetMap — for breadth and geo coordinates, then correct their two structural biases before trusting a listing: they over-include national chains (filtered by the independence rule) and they retain stale or duplicate listings (filtered by the active/closed check). These sources maximize recall but their raw output is treated as candidate leads, not verified records.

included: chain and staleness bias correction as candidates

pros.claim: Crowd directories deliver the widest first-pass net, catching businesses the curated seeds miss
pros.example: a strip-mall nail salon present on Google Maps but absent from every curated list

cons.claim: Raw crowd data is heavy with chains, duplicates, and ghost listings that pollute the census if trusted
cons.example: three Yelp entries for one cafe plus a closed location still showing five stars

failure_modes: importing chain outlets that the independence filter should remove
trusting a stale listing as an active business
acceptance_tests: harvested listings enter as candidate leads with geo coordinates and are flagged for the independence and active/closed checks before being trusted
revisit_triggers: a directory changes its data layout or access policy
a re-harvest reveals new or removed listings

base.update_signal: a crowd directory's layout, access, or listing set changes

nodes.definition: Use Instagram, Facebook, and NextDoor not as directories but as existence-and-freshness signals: an active business page, a recent post, recent reviews, or neighbor mentions corroborate that a business exists and is currently operating, and sometimes surface micro-businesses (home bakers, mobile vendors) that appear nowhere else. Their data is unstructured and self-promotional, so they confirm existence and recency but never alone establish a verified address or independence status.

pros.claim: A recent social post is often the freshest available proof a small business is still active
pros.example: a home cookie maker's weekly Instagram drop confirming current operation absent any directory entry

cons.claim: Social presence is noisy and self-promotional, easily overstating permanence or location
cons.example: a one-off pop-up posting as if it were a standing storefront

failure_modes: minting a record from a social page with no corroborating address or license
scraping private personal content rather than public business posts
acceptance_tests: social signals are recorded only as existence/freshness corroboration with a date, never as the sole source for address or independence
revisit_triggers: a platform changes public-content access
a tracked page goes dormant or reactivates

base.update_signal: a platform's public access or a tracked page's activity changes

nodes.definition: Handle sources that bot-block, return HTTP 403, or render only via JavaScript without violating their terms: reconstruct facts from search-result snippets and page titles (snippet triangulation), read cached or archived views, use alternative mirrors or the source's own structured exports/APIs where offered, and fall back to one-off manual capture for a small high-value set. The aim is lawful data recovery, never circumvention of anti-bot protections.

pros.claim: Snippet and cache triangulation recovers most needed facts from a blocked page without touching it
pros.example: reading a restaurant's address and hours from the search snippet when the live page returns 403

cons.claim: Triangulated facts are partial and can be outdated relative to the live page
cons.example: a cached snapshot showing old hours after the business changed them

failure_modes: escalating to circumvention that breaches ToS when blocked
treating a stale cached snapshot as current without dating it
acceptance_tests: each blocked-source fact is recovered by a lawful fallback (snippet, cache, mirror, official export, or manual capture) and tagged with its recovery method and date
revisit_triggers: a source tightens or relaxes its anti-bot posture
a cached or mirror source disappears

base.update_signal: a source's blocking behavior or a fallback's availability changes

nodes.definition: Merge records that refer to the same real business and split those that do not. Normalize names (drop legal suffixes, casing, punctuation), addresses (USPS-style standardization of suite and street), and phones (E.164) to canonical forms; group candidates by blocking keys (street-number+ZIP, phone prefix) to bound comparisons; then fuzzy-match within blocks on a weighted name+address+phone score, merging above a high threshold and flagging the ambiguous middle band for review.

pros.claim: Blocking plus weighted fuzzy matching deduplicates at scale without comparing every pair
pros.example: collapsing 'Joe's Tacos', 'Joes Taco Shop', and a phone-only listing into one record

cons.claim: Aggressive matching merges genuinely distinct neighbors; cautious matching leaves duplicates
cons.example: two unrelated salons in the same plaza wrongly merged on a shared suite number

failure_modes: false merge of two distinct businesses sharing an address
false split of one business listed under a DBA and a legal name
acceptance_tests: normalized name/address/phone fields exist, candidate pairs are formed within blocking keys, and a documented score threshold drives merge-versus-flag decisions
revisit_triggers: new source records arrive to reconcile
review reveals systematic false merges or splits

base.update_signal: new records arrive or match thresholds are retuned

nodes.definition: Apply the in-scope filter that keeps independents and removes chains and franchises. Operational signals of a chain/franchise: membership in a national or regional brand with many identical outlets, corporate ownership or a franchise agreement, and standardized branding not locally owned. Locally-owned single or small multi-unit operators are independent and in-scope; a franchised outlet of a national brand is out-of-scope even though a local person owns it, and is tagged with the reason it was dropped.

pros.claim: A clear franchise test prevents national outlets from inflating the independent census
pros.example: dropping a nationally-branded sandwich franchise while keeping the family-owned deli next door

cons.claim: The franchise/independent line is genuinely fuzzy for local franchisees and regional mini-chains
cons.example: a three-store local coffee brand that is arguably an independent small chain

failure_modes: keeping a national franchise because it is locally owned
dropping a legitimate local mini-chain as if it were a national chain
acceptance_tests: each record gets an independent/chain verdict with the signal that drove it, and dropped chains are retained with a drop-reason rather than silently discarded
revisit_triggers: an independent is acquired by or converts to a franchise
the in-scope definition of independence is refined

base.update_signal: a business changes ownership/franchise status or the independence rule is refined

nodes.definition: Classify each independent by premise type because each is discovered and verified differently: a storefront has a public commercial address and signage and is verifiable on the map and by visit; a home-based business operates from a residence and is found mainly via the certificate roster, FBN, or social signals rather than walk-by; a mobile/service-area business (food truck, detailer, contractor) has no fixed customer address and is verified by service-area and activity signals. The type sets which verification path applies.

pros.claim: Typing premise routes each record to the verification method that can actually confirm it
pros.example: verifying a mobile detailer by service-area and recent bookings instead of a nonexistent storefront

cons.claim: Premise type is mutable and ambiguous; a home-based business can be partly storefront-like
cons.example: a home bakery that also sells at a weekly stall, blurring home-based and mobile

failure_modes: expecting a storefront for a home-based business and marking it closed when none is found
publishing a residential address that the public record treats only as a registrant address
acceptance_tests: each record carries a premise-type tag and the verification path implied by that type is applied
revisit_triggers: a business moves from home-based to a storefront or vice versa
a mobile operator establishes a fixed location

base.update_signal: a business's premise type changes

nodes.definition: Adjudicate whether each candidate is currently operating. Freshness signals that raise the active score: recent reviews, a recent social post, current posted hours, a live phone, a valid current-year tax certificate, and an unexpired FBN; signals of closure: 'permanently closed' flags, disconnected phone, no activity across sources for an extended window, and a lapsed certificate. The rule assigns active, dormant (no recent signal but not confirmed closed), or closed, requiring at least one strong recent signal to mark active.

pros.claim: Requiring a recent strong signal to mark active keeps ghost listings out of the census
pros.example: downgrading a five-star Yelp page to closed once its phone is dead and the storefront is vacant

cons.claim: Quiet but real businesses with little online footprint get wrongly marked dormant or closed
cons.example: an old-school machine shop with no reviews and no posts that is fully operating

failure_modes: marking a low-footprint active business as closed for lack of online signal
carrying a closed business as active on a single stale source
acceptance_tests: each record gets an active/dormant/closed status backed by at least one cited recent signal, with the signal's date recorded
revisit_triggers: a fresh signal contradicts the stored status
the recency window for 'active' is retuned

base.update_signal: a fresh activity or closure signal arrives for a record

nodes.definition: Group sibling locations under one owner while keeping each premise as a distinct record. Using FBN registrant linkage, shared phone or website, and common branding, link locations to a single owner entity; then keep each physical location as its own record (so the census counts premises correctly) but attach the shared owner_id. This prevents both over-counting one business as many unrelated entries and under-counting by collapsing distinct locations into one.

pros.claim: An owner_id over distinct premise records counts locations right without losing the ownership link
pros.example: two storefronts of one local taqueria kept as two records sharing one owner_id

cons.claim: Owner-grouping signals are weak and can falsely link unrelated businesses sharing a strip-mall phone
cons.example: a shared answering service number wrongly linking two unrelated tenants

failure_modes: collapsing two real locations into one and under-counting premises
linking unrelated businesses on a coincidental shared contact
acceptance_tests: sibling locations carry a shared owner_id while remaining distinct premise records, with the linking signal cited
revisit_triggers: an owner opens or closes a location
a linkage is found to be coincidental and must be split

base.update_signal: an owner adds, closes, or reorganizes locations

nodes.definition: Attach to every record the provenance of each field — which source asserted it and when — and derive a source-agreement confidence label from how many independent sources corroborate the core facts (name, address, status) weighted by each source's reliability rank. A name confirmed by the city certificate, an FBN, and Google scores high; a name seen only on one stale directory scores low. The label travels with the record so consumers know how trustworthy each field is.

pros.claim: Field-level provenance lets a consumer trust a high-agreement address and distrust a single-source one
pros.example: a tri-source-confirmed address marked high-confidence versus a phone seen only on YellowPages

cons.claim: Agreement can be spuriously high when directories copy each other rather than observing independently
cons.example: Yelp, YellowPages, and a data aggregator all echoing one wrong address

failure_modes: counting correlated copycat sources as independent corroboration
losing the source trail so a disputed field cannot be adjudicated
acceptance_tests: every core field carries its source(s) and date, and a reliability-weighted source-agreement confidence label is computed and stored on the record
revisit_triggers: a new source corroborates or contradicts a field
source independence assumptions are revised

base.update_signal: a source is added or its independence weighting changes

nodes.definition: Model revenue for a private shop only as an explicitly labeled estimate, never as fact, because per-business revenue is not public. Take a published industry benchmark (revenue-per-employee or revenue-per-square-foot for the sector), scale it by an observable size signal (estimated headcount, storefront square footage, seat count), and emit a band tagged 'estimate, not actual' with a confidence level and a note on what would confirm it (e.g. owner disclosure, a public filing). No dollar revenue is ever stated for a named business as a fact, and no fabricated financials are produced.

included: explicit 'estimate, not actual' tag with confidence
excluded: any stated actual revenue for a named business

pros.claim: A labeled benchmark band gives a usable size sense without ever asserting a false dollar figure
pros.example: a ~6-seat cafe tagged with an industry revenue-per-seat band marked estimate, not actual, medium confidence

cons.claim: Benchmark estimates can be wildly off for an atypical business and may be misread as fact if labeling slips
cons.example: a high-margin specialty shop far above its sector's revenue-per-sqft benchmark

failure_modes: dropping the 'estimate, not actual' label so a band reads as a real figure
fabricating a precise revenue number to seem authoritative
acceptance_tests: any revenue value is a labeled benchmark band with a named ratio, the size signal used, a confidence level, and a confirmation path; no actual dollar revenue is stated for a named business
revisit_triggers: a better size signal is observed
an updated industry benchmark is published

base.update_signal: a size signal or published industry benchmark changes

nodes.definition: Define the canonical record every business must satisfy before it can be categorized: a stable id and owner_id; canonical name and any DBA; standardized address with boundary tag; phone and website; premise type; independence verdict; active/dormant/closed status with date; per-field provenance and source-agreement confidence; any labeled revenue estimate band; and a last-verified timestamp. The schema is the contract that makes records comparable, dedup-able, and gate-checkable.

pros.claim: A fixed schema makes records uniformly gate-checkable and safe to hand off
pros.example: the gate can mechanically reject any record missing a boundary tag or a status date

cons.claim: An over-strict schema can block otherwise-good records over a single hard-to-fill field
cons.example: a verified storefront stalled only because no website field exists

failure_modes: letting records through with missing required fields
schema drift so different runs emit incompatible records
acceptance_tests: the schema lists every required field with its type and which are mandatory for handoff, including provenance, status, boundary, and any labeled revenue estimate
revisit_triggers: a new required field is needed downstream
categorization changes its input contract

base.update_signal: the required-field contract changes

nodes.definition: Estimate how many independent Turlock businesses remain unseen so completeness is measured, not assumed. Treat two genuinely independent source lists (e.g. the city certificate roster versus the union of crowd directories) as two capture occasions: from the counts in each and their overlap, a Lincoln-Petersen-style estimate yields the total population and thus the unseen tail. Repeating across independent source pairs brackets the estimate and tells the run when the marginal new source adds too little to continue.

pros.claim: Capture-recapture converts 'we found a lot' into a defensible completeness percentage
pros.example: two lists of ~600 with ~400 overlap implying a population near 900 and ~33% still unseen

cons.claim: The estimate breaks when sources are not truly independent or capture probabilities differ by business type
cons.example: both lists systematically missing the same home-based segment, hiding a real gap

failure_modes: using correlated sources as the two captures and overstating completeness
ignoring heterogeneous capture so the tail is underestimated
acceptance_tests: a population and unseen-tail estimate is computed from at least one independent source pair, with the independence assumption stated and a diminishing-returns stop signal derived
revisit_triggers: a new independent source allows a fresh recapture
the population estimate shifts materially after a new ingest

base.update_signal: a new independent source enables another recapture estimate

nodes.definition: Keep the census from silently rotting by setting a re-verification cadence and staleness triggers. Records carry a last-verified timestamp; a base cadence (e.g. quarterly) requeues each record for a freshness re-check, while event triggers — a 'permanently closed' flag appearing, a certificate lapse, a new FBN, a phone going dead, or a coverage-estimate shift — requeue specific records sooner. Stale records are flagged rather than trusted, so age becomes a visible, actionable property.

pros.claim: A cadence plus triggers catches closures and moves before the census misleads consumers
pros.example: a quarterly recheck flipping a now-vacant storefront to closed within the cycle

cons.claim: Too-frequent re-verification burns effort re-confirming stable, long-lived businesses
cons.example: re-checking a 30-year hardware store every month for no change

failure_modes: no cadence so the catalog quietly drifts out of date
treating an old last-verified date as if it were current
acceptance_tests: every record has a last-verified timestamp, a base re-verification cadence exists, and event triggers requeue specific records ahead of the cadence
revisit_triggers: the cadence proves too frequent or too sparse
a new staleness signal type is identified

base.update_signal: a staleness trigger fires or the cadence is tuned

nodes.definition: Gate each verified record into categorization with an explicit definition-of-done: it satisfies the canonical schema; it is inside the geographic boundary with a tag; it passes the independence filter as in-scope; it is marked active (or explicitly carried as dormant with that flag); it has a source-agreement confidence at or above the threshold; any revenue value is a labeled estimate; and it carries a current last-verified timestamp. Records failing any condition are held in discovery with the failed condition named, never passed forward silently.

pros.claim: A definition-of-done stops half-verified records from polluting categorization downstream
pros.example: holding a record with only single-source confirmation until a second source corroborates it

cons.claim: A strict gate can starve categorization of borderline-but-real businesses that never quite clear it
cons.example: a real low-footprint shop stuck below the confidence threshold indefinitely

failure_modes: passing records that miss a required field or fall below confidence
silently dropping failed records instead of holding them with a reason
acceptance_tests: a record advances only when it meets every pass condition (schema, boundary, independence, active status, confidence threshold, labeled revenue, fresh timestamp), and failures are held with the failed condition named
revisit_triggers: the confidence threshold or required conditions change
categorization revises its intake contract

base.update_signal: the definition-of-done conditions or the categorization intake contract change

edges.why_related: the source inventory is assembled to serve the census target the goal defines
the ethics boundary scopes which sources the goal may draw on
the geographic boundary operationalizes the 'in Turlock' clause of the goal
the Chamber seed is one ranked source drawn from the inventory
the downtown list is one ranked source drawn from the inventory
the licensing census is the top-ranked ground-truth source in the inventory
FBN filings are the ownership ground-truth source ranked in the inventory
the crowd directories are the breadth sources ranked and bias-flagged in the inventory
social platforms are the freshness-signal sources ranked in the inventory
the certificate roster is used only as a public record within disclosure limits
only the public FBN fields are used; no private owner data beyond the filing
the certificate reconciliation is scoped to the city/boundary the geo rule defines
block-handling fallbacks are invoked when crowd directories bot-block or render via JS
block-handling must use lawful recovery, never circumvention of anti-bot controls
Chamber seeds are high-precision anchors fed into resolution
certificate entries are reconciled and merged during entity resolution
crowd candidate leads are deduplicated against anchors in resolution
the independence filter runs on resolved single entities, not raw duplicates
premise typing classifies a resolved entity's address situation
activity adjudication runs per resolved entity over its merged signals
recent social activity is a primary freshness signal for the active/closed rule
owner grouping operates on already-resolved distinct location records
shared FBN registrants link sibling locations to one owner
the status signals and their sources feed the source-agreement confidence
the revenue estimate's confidence is bounded by the underlying record confidence
the sector benchmark used depends on the business being an in-scope independent
the schema carries the provenance and confidence fields the record must hold
capture-recapture counts operate over schema-conformant resolved records
the last-verified field that the cadence ages lives in the schema
re-verification re-runs the active/closed check on aged records
the gate checks each record against the canonical schema
the completeness estimate decides when the census as a whole is ready to hand off
a staleness trigger requeues a record back through activity adjudication
a large estimated unseen tail sends the run back to add or re-rank sources
the authoritative certificate roster and a stale crowd listing can disagree on whether a business exists or is open
edges.resolution_rule: prefer the higher-ranked source for the disputed field: a current certificate overrides a stale directory on existence, but a fresh directory/social signal can override the roster on current status

edges.why_related: dropping franchise outlets shrinks the kept set even as recapture estimates a larger total population including those out-of-scope entries
edges.resolution_rule: compute capture-recapture only over the in-scope independent set so the completeness percentage measures independents, not all businesses

edges.why_related: an expired FBN can imply closure while fresh social or review signals show the business is still operating
edges.resolution_rule: treat an expired FBN as a weak closure signal only; a single strong recent activity signal overrides it and marks the business active

edges.why_related: the independence verdict and its sector determine which revenue benchmark is applied

conflict_axes.name: recall_breadth_vs_precision_noise
conflict_axes.description: Broad crowd directories maximize recall but inject chains, duplicates, and ghost listings, while curated seeds are precise but partial.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat crowd listings as candidate leads filtered by the independence and active/closed checks, anchored to curated and licensing seeds

conflict_axes.name: authoritative_lag_vs_fresh_noise
conflict_axes.description: Authoritative records (certificates, FBN) are trustworthy but lag real status; fresh signals (social, reviews) are current but noisy and self-promotional.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use authoritative sources for existence and ownership, fresh signals for current status, and reconcile per field

conflict_axes.name: aggressive_merge_vs_cautious_split
conflict_axes.description: Aggressive entity matching collapses duplicates but risks false merges; cautious matching avoids false merges but leaves duplicates inflating the count.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: merge only above a high weighted-match threshold and route the ambiguous band to review rather than auto-deciding

conflict_axes.name: completeness_push_vs_stop_cost
conflict_axes.description: Chasing the last few percent of the unseen tail costs disproportionate effort against a near-complete census that is good enough to hand off.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: stop when capture-recapture shows the unseen tail below threshold and the marginal new source adds little

conflict_axes.name: data_recovery_vs_tos_respect
conflict_axes.description: Recovering data from a bot-blocked or JS-only page conflicts with respecting the source's terms and anti-bot controls.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use only lawful fallbacks (snippet, cache, mirror, official export, manual capture); never circumvent protections

conflict_axes.name: owner_linkage_value_vs_privacy
conflict_axes.description: Linking businesses to owners adds analytic value but pressures the boundary against collecting private personal owner data.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: link owners only via public FBN/certificate fields and never store private owner detail beyond those records

conflict_axes.name: strict_boundary_vs_fringe_inclusion
conflict_axes.description: Restricting to city limits is clean but drops Turlock-identifying fringe businesses; including the ZIP/fringe widens coverage but admits non-city entities.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: tag every record in-city/in-ZIP/fringe so the fringe can be included or excluded without re-running discovery

conflict_axes.name: estimate_usefulness_vs_factual_honesty
conflict_axes.description: A revenue estimate is useful for sizing but risks being read as a factual figure for a private business whose revenue is not public.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: emit only a labeled benchmark band tagged 'estimate, not actual' with confidence and a confirmation path

conflict_axes.name: strict_gate_vs_throughput
conflict_axes.description: A strict definition-of-done protects categorization from bad records but can starve it of borderline-but-real businesses.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hold failing records with the named failed condition for re-verification rather than dropping or force-passing them

conflict_axes.name: verification_freshness_vs_effort
conflict_axes.description: Frequent re-verification keeps the catalog current but wastes effort re-confirming stable long-lived businesses.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: run a modest base cadence and let event triggers requeue specific records sooner

edge_cases.description: A business appears on Yelp and Google but the storefront is vacant and the phone is dead
edge_cases.trigger: crowd listings show a business that has actually closed
edge_cases.mitigation: require a recent strong activity signal to mark active; absent it, downgrade to dormant or closed with the dead-phone evidence dated

edge_cases.description: Two unrelated businesses share a suite number in the same plaza and fuzzy-match as one
edge_cases.trigger: address normalization collides distinct tenants on a shared suite
edge_cases.mitigation: require name and phone agreement, not address alone, above the merge threshold and flag suite-only matches for review

edge_cases.description: A locally-owned national franchise outlet looks independent because the owner is a local resident
edge_cases.trigger: a franchisee of a national brand is locally owned
edge_cases.mitigation: drop as out-of-scope on the franchise-agreement and national-branding signals despite local ownership, tagging the drop reason

edge_cases.description: A home-based business has no storefront and is marked closed because none is found on the map
edge_cases.trigger: verification expects a storefront for a home-based business
edge_cases.mitigation: type it home-based first and verify via certificate, FBN, and social activity rather than a storefront visit

edge_cases.description: A crowd directory returns HTTP 403 and the listing renders only via JavaScript
edge_cases.trigger: a bot-blocked or JS-only source page
edge_cases.mitigation: recover the facts via snippet, cached view, mirror, or official export and tag the recovery method and date, never circumventing the block

edge_cases.description: The city certificate roster shows a certificate still on file months after the shop closed
edge_cases.trigger: a lagging authoritative record contradicts fresh closure signals
edge_cases.mitigation: let a fresh closure signal override the lagging roster on current status while keeping the roster as the existence record

edge_cases.description: Three directories echo the same wrong address, creating false high agreement
edge_cases.trigger: correlated copycat sources are counted as independent corroboration
edge_cases.mitigation: discount correlated aggregator sources in the agreement weighting and require an authoritative source to confirm a disputed address

edge_cases.description: An active machine shop with no reviews, posts, or website is wrongly marked dormant
edge_cases.trigger: a real low-online-footprint business lacks fresh signals
edge_cases.mitigation: accept a current tax certificate or a live phone as a sufficient activity signal so offline-but-real businesses stay active

edge_cases.description: A revenue band is shown without its 'estimate, not actual' label and reads as a real figure
edge_cases.trigger: the estimate label is dropped in output
edge_cases.mitigation: make the 'estimate, not actual' tag, the benchmark, and the confidence mandatory schema fields that the gate enforces

edge_cases.description: A 95380 address actually sits in unincorporated county, not the city
edge_cases.trigger: ZIP is used as a proxy for city limits
edge_cases.mitigation: tag it in-ZIP/fringe rather than in-city and let the consumer decide whether to include the fringe

edge_cases.description: Both the certificate roster and the crowd directories miss the same home-based segment, hiding a coverage gap
edge_cases.trigger: the two capture sources are not independent for one business class
edge_cases.mitigation: estimate capture separately by premise type and add a source (social, FBN) that captures the missed class before claiming completeness

edge_cases.description: A business with only a single stale-source listing is pushed to categorization
edge_cases.trigger: a record below the confidence threshold reaches the handoff gate
edge_cases.mitigation: hold it in discovery with 'below confidence threshold' named and requeue for a second-source confirmation

workflow.action: Define the census target and stop condition
workflow.description: Fix the in-scope universe and the completeness threshold that ends the run
workflow.gate: the positive in-scope test, boundary and independence references, and a numeric stop condition are stated

workflow.action: Inventory and reliability-rank the public sources
workflow.description: List every source with its rank, bias, and trusted role
workflow.gate: each source has a rank, a bias note, and an assigned role

workflow.action: Set the ethics and geographic boundaries
workflow.description: Define public-data-only limits and the city/ZIP/fringe boundary rule
workflow.gate: the public-data rule and the in-city/in-ZIP/fringe tag rule are documented

workflow.description: Load Chamber and downtown-association listings as high-precision anchors
workflow.gate: seed records carry name, address, and source tag and are marked partial-coverage

workflow.action: Obtain and reconcile the licensing and ownership ground-truth
workflow.description: Request the city certificate roster and pull county FBN filings, reconciling against seeds
workflow.gate: the certificate roster is obtained and certificate-only and directory-only lists exist

workflow.action: Harvest crowd directories and handle blocked sources
workflow.description: Pull broad listings with geo, recovering blocked-source facts lawfully
workflow.artifact: candidate-lead pool with geo and recovery tags
workflow.gate: leads carry geo coordinates and blocked-source facts are tagged with their recovery method

workflow.action: Resolve entities and deduplicate across sources
workflow.description: Normalize and fuzzy-match within blocking keys to merge duplicates
workflow.gate: normalized fields exist and a documented threshold drives merge-versus-flag decisions

workflow.action: Classify independence, premise type, and activity status
workflow.description: Apply the independence filter, premise typing, and active/closed adjudication
workflow.gate: each record has an independence verdict, premise type, and a status backed by a dated signal

workflow.action: Consolidate owners and attach provenance and revenue estimates
workflow.description: Group owner siblings, attach field provenance and confidence, add labeled revenue bands
workflow.gate: each record has source-agreement confidence and any revenue value is a labeled estimate band

workflow.action: Assemble records against the canonical schema
workflow.description: Populate every required field into the canonical record contract
workflow.gate: every required field is present with its type for each record

workflow.action: Estimate coverage and set the freshness cadence
workflow.description: Run capture-recapture over independents and schedule re-verification
workflow.gate: an unseen-tail estimate over the in-scope set and a re-verification cadence with triggers exist

workflow.description: Pass only records meeting the definition-of-done; hold the rest with reasons
workflow.gate: advancing records meet every pass condition and failures are held with the named failed condition

dominance_rules.rule: Public-data-and-ToS ethics dominates every collection choice
dominance_rules.rationale: a single ToS or privacy breach can invalidate the whole census and expose liability
dominance_rules.trigger: any source access or owner-data decision
dominance_rules.action: block any collection that breaches ToS or stores private owner data beyond public records

dominance_rules.rule: Authoritative ground-truth dominates crowd sources on existence and ownership
dominance_rules.rationale: certificates and FBN filings are verified records while crowd listings are unverified
dominance_rules.trigger: a crowd listing disagrees with the certificate or FBN on whether a business exists or who owns it
dominance_rules.action: trust the authoritative record for existence and ownership

dominance_rules.rule: A fresh strong activity signal dominates a lagging authoritative status
dominance_rules.rationale: rosters and FBN expiry lag real-world opening and closing
dominance_rules.trigger: fresh activity contradicts a lagging certificate or expired FBN on current status
dominance_rules.action: let the fresh signal set current status while keeping the authoritative existence record

dominance_rules.rule: The independence filter dominates inclusion regardless of recall pressure
dominance_rules.rationale: chains and franchises are out of scope no matter how easily found
dominance_rules.trigger: a franchise or chain outlet is a candidate for inclusion
dominance_rules.action: drop it as out-of-scope with a tagged drop reason

dominance_rules.rule: Labeled-estimate honesty dominates any demand for a revenue figure
dominance_rules.rationale: private revenue is not public and must never be asserted as fact
dominance_rules.trigger: a revenue value is requested or emitted
dominance_rules.action: emit only a labeled benchmark band with confidence and a confirmation path, never an actual figure

dominance_rules.rule: The high merge threshold dominates the urge to collapse near-matches
dominance_rules.rationale: a false merge silently loses a real business and corrupts the count
dominance_rules.trigger: two records match only on a weak shared signal like a suite number
dominance_rules.action: hold the pair for review rather than auto-merging

dominance_rules.rule: In-scope capture-recapture dominates whole-population counting for completeness
dominance_rules.rationale: completeness is about independents, not all businesses including dropped chains
dominance_rules.action: run the estimate only over the in-scope independent set

dominance_rules.rationale: a bad record poisons categorization more than a delayed good one
dominance_rules.trigger: a record fails any pass condition at the gate
dominance_rules.action: hold it with the named failed condition instead of passing it forward

anti_rework_rules.rule: Reliability-rank sources before merging any of their records
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a noisy directory overriding authoritative ground-truth and forcing a later re-merge

anti_rework_rules.rule: Normalize name, address, and phone before fuzzy matching
anti_rework_rules.prevents: false merges and splits that must be unpicked downstream

anti_rework_rules.rule: Type premise (storefront/home/mobile) before adjudicating active versus closed
anti_rework_rules.prevents: marking home-based and mobile businesses closed for lacking a storefront

anti_rework_rules.rule: Request the city certificate roster early in the run
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discovering the long-tail licensing layer only after the crowd harvest is already 'done'

anti_rework_rules.rule: Use only lawful fallbacks for blocked sources from the start
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a ToS-breaching scrape that taints records and must be discarded

anti_rework_rules.rule: Make the 'estimate, not actual' revenue tag a mandatory schema field
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an unlabeled band being read as fact and having to be retracted

anti_rework_rules.rule: Compute capture-recapture only over the in-scope independent set
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a completeness figure inflated by out-of-scope chains that must be recomputed

anti_rework_rules.rule: Set the re-verification cadence when records are first assembled
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a stale catalog that must be re-verified wholesale later

iteration_protocol.trigger: the coverage estimate shows a large unseen tail
iteration_protocol.action: add or re-rank sources and re-harvest before claiming completeness

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new public source or an updated roster becomes available
iteration_protocol.action: ingest it, re-resolve entities, and recompute coverage

iteration_protocol.trigger: review reveals systematic false merges or splits
iteration_protocol.action: retune normalization and match thresholds and re-run resolution

iteration_protocol.trigger: a staleness trigger fires for a record (closure flag, lapsed certificate, dead phone)
iteration_protocol.action: requeue the record through activity adjudication and update its status and timestamp

iteration_protocol.trigger: a business changes ownership or franchise status
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the independence filter and owner consolidation for it
revise the schema and the definition-of-done and re-gate held records

iteration_protocol.trigger: a source ToS or privacy rule changes
iteration_protocol.action: re-scope collection from that source and purge any now-disallowed fields

priority_rationale: The frame nodes (goal, source inventory, ethics, boundary) come first because every downstream choice depends on knowing the target, the trusted sources, the legal limits, and what counts as Turlock; ingestion and harvesting feed entity resolution, which must precede all classification; classification, provenance, owner consolidation, and labeled revenue estimation enrich resolved entities into the canonical schema; and coverage estimation, freshness cadence, and the handoff gate come last because they compose the assembled records into a measured, maintained, gate-checked census ready for categorization.
